page.layout: One block of verse on one printed page: running head at the top with page number at the top right; the poem in stanzas, full width, with no marginal notes.

p.i: Non terret illum pauperies inops, Nec inflat auri copia largior, Aequam secundis rebus, & asperis Seruare mentem nouit, & undique Vexationum si violentior Procella tentat, Tartarasi mouent Infesta turbas, impauidus manet.

Illum tuetur dextera Caelitum, Certasque semper prouida semitas, Monstrat, minaci nec sinit obrui Tentationum turbine grandium: Si forte nutat, si pede lubricos Quandoque calles ambigúo terit, Presssum periclis omnibus explicat.

Hac esse nostei sera satis docet. Abramus: ex quo Patris Olympici Fidelis illum cura tegit, licet Multis petatur saepe malis, tamen Hac cuncta vincit maiorvatrocia. Si damna crescunt, indomiti simul Augentur illi robora pectoris.
Natale quondam deserutt solum: Fetuens coegit sollicitum fames Aegyptiorum littora visere.

page.notes: Several words in the verse are blurred by stains and show-through; "Tartarasi", "nostei", "Abramus", "maiorvatrocia" and "Vexationum" are doubtful readings. "Presssum" and "deserutt" may be misprints. Greek-style ligatures "&" kept as printed.
